question: Design review. Kafka 4.3.2 on VMs, KRaft, nine brokers spread over three zones. We are introducing tiered storage with a third-party RemoteStorageManager plugin for our S3-compatible object store (remote.log.storage.system.enable=true on the brokers). Topic order-events: 48 partitions, about 60 MB/s on average, retention.ms 30 days, replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas 2, producers use acks=all. Today that is about 155 TB per copy, 466 TB of local disk. The plan: remote.storage.enable=true with local.retention.ms of 6 hours, and at the same time replication factor 2 and min.insync.replicas 1, 'because the object store keeps the data eleven-nines durable, so the brokers are only a cache'. Does the plan hold? What would you change, and how much local disk will we need?

Please review this KafkaTopic change before we merge it. Strimzi 1.3.1, Kafka 4.3.2. api-keys is a compacted topic (key = API key id, value = the key's metadata and status); when a customer revokes a key we write a tombstone for it. Each of our 40 api-gateway pods builds its in-memory key map by reading api-keys from offset 0 with assign() when it starts, then follows the head. After a year of churn that initial read takes 40 to 55 minutes, and pods start on every deploy and node rotation. The PR author wants faster starts: 'tombstones are useless once compaction has removed the old values, so drop them straight away; roll a segment every minute so the cleaner works continuously; and clean more aggressively.'

Topic shipment-status: 36 partitions, replication factor 3, min.insync.replicas=1 at topic level (set years ago 'for availability'); the carrier producers use acks=1. question: Kafka 4.3.2 on VMs, KRaft, six brokers; the cluster was created on 4.2.0 and its cluster-level min.insync.replicas is 2. Last month the ledger team set min.insync.replicas=3 on their topic ledger-entries (12 partitions, replication factor 3) 'for maximum durability'. Since then every monthly patch run, which restarts one broker at a time, makes their writer (acks=all) fail with NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS for a couple of minutes per broker, each time on the partitions that have a replica on the restarting broker. The brokers' disks are at 70%, so a fourth replica is not an option. The team wants to lower it to 2; our platform lead's rule is 'never lower min.insync.replicas'. Who is right, and if we change it, how?
